rule: A question in 'easier' is skipped once the latest attempt on anything in 'harder' passed (85%): the harder one already does the easier one's calculation, plus more steps. Refs are a node id, or node#variantId for one variant. Hand-authored; tests/supersedes.test.mjs checks every ref exists and nothing loops.

pairs.why: The activity-coefficient question starts by finding I for the same single salts.
Finding I for a mixture of salts is the first step of the pH and Fe3+/Fe2+ activity questions.
Every one of these needs I, then gamma from Debye-Hückel, then an activity, which is the whole of the gamma question.
A cell potential is two half-cell Nernst calculations with activities, then a difference.
The Zn / Fe3+,Fe2+ cell contains the Fe3+/Fe2+ half-cell with activities.
The salt version does I, gamma(H+) and pH from activity as well, with more ions in the ionic strength.
Two metal half-cells with activities are a subset of the Zn / Fe3+,Fe2+ cell.
The overall PSI is three sub-index calculations and a maximum.
Reading an activity from two potentials needs the Nernstian slope for that charge.
The dilution chain begins with reading a concentration off the calibration line.
The ammonia chain is the same calibration and dilutions with a negative slope and a Kjeldahl step on the end.
Same back-calculation, one dilution step instead of two.
The short version is parts (a) to (c) of the full chain, word for word.
Adding or subtracting two terms is the same rule as three, with fewer terms.
The wider-peaks question computes the same R_S first, then recomputes it.
Concentration from absorbance is the first step of the dilution question.
The confidence interval starts from the mean and s of the replicates.
